memos.headline: S10 and S04 Lead on Trend and Relative Strength; S02 and S06 Breaking Down
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of October 2. S10 sits just 0.8% off its 52-week high with +7.2% above its 50-day mean, +16.6% above its 200-day mean, and the strongest 4-week relative strength vs SPY at +2.9%—this is the cleanest uptrend in the group. S04 is similarly strong with a massive +32.3% 12-week relative strength vs SPY and RSI at 62.6, though its +6.1% extension above the 50-day makes me slightly cautious on entry timing. On the other side, S02 and S06 are in clear downtrends: S02 is -14.8% off its high with RSI 40.4 and -16.2% 12-week relative strength vs SPY, while S06 prints an RSI of 34.5 with -8.2% over four weeks and -7.7% relative underperformance. I would need S02 to reclaim its 50-day mean (~$393) and S06 to stabilize above 340 before reconsidering those names.

views.note: Near 52-week highs with strong trend structure across all timeframes; I'd reconsider below the 50-day mean (~$218).
Exceptional 12-week relative strength of +32.3% vs SPY and healthy RSI of 62.6, but +6.1% above 50-day warrants patience on sizing; invalidated below ~$488.
Only -2.2% from 52-week high, well above both moving averages with moderate RSI of 54.7; would exit on a break below ~$322 (50-day area).
Strong 12-week relative strength of +16.9% vs SPY and above both averages, but the negative 26-week return of -4.1% tempers conviction; watch 160 support.
RSI 34.5 is the lowest in the universe, -8.2% over 4 weeks with accelerating relative weakness; no reason to step in until price reclaims ~$350.
Down -13.8% over 12 weeks with -16.2% relative strength vs SPY, trading well below its 50-day mean; trend is clearly broken.
Flat near its 50-day mean with RSI 50 and -14.7% drawdown—no directional edge; would get interested on a move above $370.
Trading below its 200-day mean by -1.9% with negative relative strength across all windows; structurally the weakest longer-term trend.
Sitting -2.0% below 50-day mean with -11.4% drawdown and near-flat relative strength; needs to hold ~$245 or risk joining the laggards.
Bouncing with +5.7% over 4 weeks but still -20.6% from 52-week high and -12.3% 12-week relative strength; could be a bear-market rally until ~$900 is reclaimed.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Lead on Earnings Power; S09 and S01 Flash Warning Signs on Margin Compression
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe between names with explosive, durable earnings growth and those suffering margin erosion. S10 stands out with 106% YoY revenue growth, a 62% net margin, and modest $33.4B debt—this is the strongest fundamental profile in the group. S05 is similarly extraordinary: 93.7% net margin, 24% revenue growth, and only $14.8B in debt, though the margin level invites scrutiny on sustainability. On the other end, S09 posted just 4.9% net margin with net income down 45.8% YoY on anemic 2.4% revenue growth, and S01 saw net income decline 15.8% on essentially flat revenue (+1.5%), with $29.3B in debt against only $21.2B in annual revenue. I would need to see margin stabilization or a clear inflection in operating cash flow at S09 and S01 before getting constructive. S03's 244.9% net income growth is eye-catching, but I note $133B in total debt and want to see whether that earnings surge is recurring or one-time before adding conviction.

views.note: Revenue doubling YoY with 62% net margin and manageable $33.4B debt is the best earnings-power profile in the universe; a deceleration below 30% revenue growth would change my view.
93.7% net margin and 24% revenue growth on minimal debt is exceptional, though I flag that margin sustainability is the key risk to monitor.
39.7% net margin, 17.7% revenue growth, and 31.3% net income growth with only $40.3B debt represent high-quality compounding; margin contraction below 35% would be a concern.
24% revenue growth and 64.9% net income growth with 17.5% net margin show improving operating leverage, though $36.2B debt on $20.5B revenue warrants monitoring.
244.9% net income growth is striking but $133B in total debt and the need to confirm earnings durability keep me on the sideline until the next quarter clarifies the trajectory.
27.7% revenue growth and 36.9% net margin are solid, but $460.5B in total debt is an outsized leverage position that compresses my confidence in durable free cash flow.
16.4% revenue growth and 27.2% net margin are respectable but $82.3B in debt and decelerating growth relative to peers leave me waiting for a better entry.
Flat revenue (+0.4%) and a thin 4.9% net margin with $73.3B in debt signal weak earnings power; I need to see top-line reacceleration above mid-single digits.
Net income down 45.8% YoY on 2.4% revenue growth with a 4.9% net margin is clear cash-flow compression; I would reconsider only if margins recover above 8%.
Net income declining 15.8% on 1.5% revenue growth with $29.3B debt against $21.2B revenue signals deteriorating earnings power; operating cash flow improvement would change my view.

memos.headline: Surging 10y Yields and Sticky 3.4% CPI Signal a Hawkish Pause Regime — Favor Banks and Staples, Avoid Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see a regime best described as a hawkish pause with upside inflation risk. The Fed raised the upper bound 25bp over the past three months to 4.00%, yet CPI is running at 3.4% YoY with essentially zero momentum over the last three months — inflation is sticky, not falling. The 10y yield has surged 79bp in three months to 5.28%, a punishing move for anything duration-sensitive, while the 10-2 spread steepened modestly to +46bp, consistent with the market pricing in higher-for-longer rates and possibly a term premium repricing. The labor market remains solid at 4.1% unemployment, down 20bp over both 3- and 12-month horizons, which gives the Fed no urgency to ease. A regime shift would require either a sharp CPI deceleration below 2.5% YoY or unemployment breaking above 4.5%, neither of which is in the data today.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth equities face severe headwinds with 10y at 5.28% and rising; discount rates are compressing valuations.
Banks benefit from a positively sloped curve (+46bp 10-2 spread) and higher-for-longer rates supporting net interest margins.
Staples offer defensive positioning in a hawkish-pause regime with sticky inflation and solid employment supporting consumer spending on essentials.
Energy is a mixed bag — solid labor market supports demand, but surging real rates could weigh on capex-heavy names; staying neutral until clearer direction.
High-duration growth names are most vulnerable to the 118bp YoY rise in 10y yields; I would underweight until the rate trajectory stabilizes.
Cyclicals face cross-currents: strong labor market is supportive but rising yields and sticky inflation could slow activity; no strong conviction either way.
Rate-sensitive sectors face continued pressure as the Fed shows no inclination to ease with CPI at 3.4% and unemployment at 4.1%.

memos.headline: S10 Positive Earnings Reaction Stands Out; Leadership Turnover at S08 and S03 Warrants Caution
memos.body: I see the clearest sentiment signal in S10, which posted an +8.7% price reaction on its 8-K results filing on 2026-08-26, followed by a material agreement and an Other Events filing—three filings in roughly two weeks suggest an active narrative that the market is rewarding. S08 and S03 both filed director/officer departure or appointment 8-Ks in early September; leadership churn without accompanying positive catalysts tilts tone negative and I would avoid until clarity emerges. S07 entered a material definitive agreement and created a direct financial obligation on 2026-09-01, which is a mixed signal—new financing can be constructive or dilutive—so I stay neutral pending further detail. S04 and S02 each filed Reg FD disclosures in early September; these are routine investor-communication events with no discernible tone shift, leaving me neutral on both.

views.note: Three 8-Ks in two weeks including an earnings release that drove +8.7% suggests a positive narrative shift still building.
Director/officer departure 8-K/A with no offsetting positive catalyst signals potential governance uncertainty.
Two filings in a week—one a leadership change—without a clear positive event suggest unsettled tone.
New material agreement and direct financial obligation could be constructive or dilutive; tone is ambiguous.
Reg FD disclosure is routine investor communication with no discernible sentiment shift.
Single Reg FD filing offers no meaningful tone change to trade around.
Other Events filing from mid-August is stale and generated no notable price or tone signal.

memos.headline: WTI at $99.77 (+43% in 3 months) signals a structural energy-security shock; credit spreads widening in tandem
memos.body: I am focused on the extraordinary 43% three-month surge in WTI crude to $99.77/bbl, which is the dominant geopolitical signal in today's data. While the Economic Policy Uncertainty index has actually fallen 25% over three months to 156, the combination of near-$100 oil and a 50 bp widening in HY OAS over the same period tells me the oil move is supply-driven—likely reflecting sanctions enforcement, OPEC discipline, or a regional conflict disrupting flows—rather than demand-pull. The VIX at 16.39 is remarkably sanguine, which I read as equity markets not yet pricing the margin compression that $100 oil implies for energy-intensive sectors. I have higher conviction on energy-exposed names (beneficiaries and victims) and lower conviction on names where the 8-K filings give me no geopolitical detail beyond item headers. A reversal in oil—say a sanctions waiver or SPR release pushing WTI below $85—would change my view materially.

views.note: Energy-sector names benefit directly from near-$100 WTI; structural supply tightness supports prices absent a policy reversal.
Recent 8-K (Other Events, Sep 14) provides no geopolitical clarity; elevated oil is a headwind if S03 is energy-consuming, but I lack detail to take a directional view.
Reg FD disclosure in early September offers no actionable geopolitical content; widening HY spreads (+59 bp 1m) warrant caution for leveraged names.
Two 8-Ks in quick succession (Aug-Sep) suggest corporate activity, but without substance I cannot assess geopolitical exposure; oil-cost sensitivity is the key unknown.
Reg FD filing in September is opaque; the benign VIX masks rising credit risk (HY OAS +50 bp 3m), so I stay on the sideline.
With oil up 43% in three months and HY spreads widening, energy-intensive or leveraged industrials face margin and funding pressure; the Aug 8-K gives no offsetting positive signal.
No company-specific filings in evidence; the macro backdrop of surging oil and widening credit spreads is unfavorable for names without clear energy-beneficiary status.
